title: Share one value-embedding table across all VE layers
description: Replaced the 5 per-layer value_embeds tables with a single nn.Embedding looked up once per forward and handed to the same alternating layers (net -4 lines); VE params 26.2M -> 5.2M, model 85.9M -> 64.9M, FLOPs/token unchanged.
reflection: NEGATIVE: val_bpb 0.984022 vs the 0.981817 baseline, +0.0022 (~2.7 sigma on the round-3/4 arm-to-arm sd of 8e-4). Mean-last-60 train loss 2.7638 vs the baseline's 2.758 agrees, so it is optimization/representation, not eval noise. The comparison is unusually clean because throughput barely moved: 1174 steps / 307.8M tokens vs 1168 / 306.2M (+0.5%), MFU 41.21% vs 41.00%, VRAM 66.4GB vs 67.8GB. Two conclusions. (1) The predicted throughput win from 1 gather + 1 backward scatter instead of 5 is ~0.5% of tokens, i.e. nothing - embedding gather/scatter is not a measurable share of this step. (2) My mechanism - 'each row gets 5x the gradient signal, which must help at 1150 steps' - is wrong, or at least is outweighed: per-layer value-embedding specialisation is load-bearing, and the 21M-param cut is NOT free here even though a5's matched dim-512 pair showed a same-sized cut as free. The difference is that the dim cut bought 32% more tokens and this one bought 0.5%, which is the cell's recurring pattern: a parameter cut only breaks even when it is paid back in data. Combined with a0's VE-on-every-layer arm this round, the VE axis should be read as: coverage and per-layer identity of the tables are what matter, table count is not a free knob to shrink.
